data.name: Jobous the alien R
data.detailed_description:
Travel trugh space with a big laser gun, and lot of wacky enemies and obstacles.

Jobous the alien R is an addictive space shooter with a cute alien named Jobous. its just like an old-school arcade space shooter , but with an insane difficulty.
the goal of the game is to get from point A to point B without crashing in anything or anyone. luckily its many power ups to help you stay alive.

This is the type of game you will never complete. It is so hard that not only will your hand sweat. It will also fall off in the process
. you will cry for your mother and praying to god, just to complete one level. Are you up for the challenge?

(in other words a rage game)

STORY:

The story is sweet and simple. Jobous and his wife is living the dream in outer space. When suddenly ( dramatic music ) his wife want some new shoes. Oh no she is going to use all their space money (jup she is kinda a money spender). Jobous

Immediately panics. What should he do? Jobous takes his ship and travel after her. Can he save his wife from spending all their space money on shoes?

reviews.review:
Jobous the alien R is a quirky and deliberately punishing arcade-style space shooter that combines absurd humor, simple mechanics, and an overwhelming emphasis on survival. Developed and published by Veibyn, the game embraces the philosophy of classic arcade experiences, where success depends on quick reflexes, patience, and the willingness to repeat difficult sections. Rather than attempting to impress players with elaborate storytelling or sophisticated gameplay systems, it delivers a straightforward challenge involving a small alien navigating dangerous environments. Its lighthearted appearance creates an amusing contrast with its unforgiving difficulty, making it particularly appealing to players who enjoy testing their limits.

The story follows Jobous, an adorable extraterrestrial whose peaceful existence takes an unexpected turn when his wife decides to purchase new shoes. Worried that her shopping habits will exhaust their savings, he immediately boards his spaceship and pursues her across space. This ridiculous premise establishes the game's comedic identity without requiring complicated dialogue or extensive narrative development. Although the storyline serves primarily as an excuse for the action, its unusual domestic conflict provides personality and distinguishes the adventure from conventional science-fiction shooters. Players looking for a meaningful narrative may find it underdeveloped, but the humor complements the intentionally chaotic nature of the experience.

Gameplay focuses on guiding a spaceship through hazardous environments while avoiding collisions with enemies and obstacles. Equipped with a powerful laser weapon, Jobous must travel between designated points without being destroyed along the way. While the basic mechanics sound uncomplicated, the challenge comes from maintaining precise movement and reacting quickly to surrounding dangers. Combat is only one part of the experience, as successfully navigating obstacles is equally important. The game encourages careful positioning, environmental awareness, and persistence rather than reckless aggression. This straightforward design makes the objective immediately understandable, although mastering the necessary movements is considerably more demanding.

The most distinctive feature is its extreme difficulty. The game openly presents itself as a rage-inducing experience, suggesting that even completing individual levels can become an exhausting undertaking. Frequent failures are central to its intended appeal, encouraging players to learn from mistakes and gradually develop better strategies. This approach can create rewarding moments when previously troublesome sections are finally overcome. However, difficulty alone does not guarantee entertainment. Players who dislike repetition or expect a forgiving progression system may quickly become frustrated. The experience is therefore best suited to individuals who enjoy challenging arcade games and consider perseverance an essential part of the fun.

Power-ups introduce an additional layer of assistance, giving players opportunities to improve their survival chances during dangerous encounters. Their inclusion helps prevent the gameplay from relying entirely on movement and shooting skills. Collecting beneficial enhancements can potentially provide temporary advantages when confronting particularly troublesome obstacles. Nevertheless, the available description does not elaborate on the complete selection of power-ups or their specific functions. The concept remains promising because it adds another consideration to an otherwise straightforward formula, although the overall depth of the system is difficult to judge without more detailed information.

Visually, the game adopts a playful science-fiction identity built around its cute protagonist, unusual enemies, and exaggerated premise. Its presentation emphasizes personality over realism, which suits the ridiculous storyline and arcade-inspired design. The combination of charming imagery and relentless difficulty gives the experience an entertaining contradiction. However, its modest scope means players should approach it as a small independent production rather than expect elaborate environments, extensive visual effects, or cinematic presentation. The available information also provides limited insight into soundtrack quality and animation variety, preventing a definitive assessment of those elements.

Replayability largely depends on the player's enthusiasm for mastering difficult challenges. Rather than advertising extensive customization, complex character development, or multiple gameplay modes, the experience concentrates on reaching objectives despite increasingly demanding obstacles. This focused structure can appeal to arcade enthusiasts who enjoy improving their performance through repeated attempts. Conversely, players seeking substantial mechanical variety or additional activities may find the formula restrictive. The absence of prominently advertised progression systems also makes the satisfaction of overcoming difficult sections especially important to the game's lasting appeal.

Technical requirements are exceptionally modest, with an Intel Core i3 processor, GeForce GTS 150 graphics card, and approximately 27 MB of storage listed as minimum specifications. These requirements suggest that the game should be relatively undemanding on compatible Windows computers. Steam Cloud functionality is also supported, providing convenience for players who use multiple systems. Regarding Steam Deck compatibility, the game currently has no confirmed official Verified or Playable classification, so its status should be considered Unknown or Unverified. Although its lightweight requirements are encouraging, successful operation through Proton and proper handheld control functionality cannot be guaranteed without testing.

One notable limitation is the relatively small amount of community feedback available. With only a handful of Steam user reviews, the game has not accumulated enough evaluations to establish an official overall review score. This makes it harder to determine how consistently its difficulty, controls, and level design satisfy players. Its inexpensive price makes experimentation more approachable, but prospective buyers should understand that its deliberately frustrating design is a central feature rather than an occasional inconvenience. Those expecting a relaxing space shooter will probably find its demanding nature unsuitable.

Overall, Jobous the alien R offers a peculiar mixture of comedy, arcade shooting, and relentless difficulty. Its greatest strengths are its amusing premise, accessible objectives, lightweight technical requirements, and commitment to providing a demanding challenge. Its weaknesses include limited advertised gameplay variety, minimal narrative depth, and an unforgiving structure that may become repetitive. It is a niche experience that prioritizes persistence over accessibility and simple entertainment over ambitious design. For players who appreciate unconventional independent games and enjoy conquering frustrating obstacles, it offers a reasonably entertaining distraction.

It is a modest but distinctive arcade shooter with enough personality to attract dedicated challenge seekers, although its narrow scope and extreme difficulty limit its broader appeal.

Rating: 6/10
